clue.text: Kinds of food eaten by wealthy German actress

indicators.note: by here means next to, so the food sits beside the wealthy word

parts.note: a diet is the kind of food a person habitually eats
wealthy means rich

explanation.surface: Someone reports what sort of meals a moneyed German film star eats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eaten by' looks like a container instruction, but 'eaten' belongs to the food phrase and 'by' simply places it beside RICH.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlene Dietrich was a celebrated German-born film actress and singer.

clue.text: Irving and others as four royal characters in 13

definitions.meaning: the actor Sir Henry Irving and others sharing his first name
Shakespeare (13 across) wrote plays about four kings of that name: the fourth, fifth, sixth and eighth

explanation.definitionFit: The plural first name covers both people called like Irving and the kings in the history plays.

clue.text: Secure article supporting English craft of musical theatre

parts.note: to secure something is to pin it
a is the indefinite article
being for something means supporting it

explanation.surface: Someone fastens an item that props up a piece of English theatrical handiwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests skill, but it means a vessel: HMS Pinafore is the ship in the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta.
explanation.definitionFit: HMS Pinafore is the fictional warship giving its name to a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera.

clue.text: A line inserted in excellent last act

indicators.note: inserted in tells us the first pieces go inside the word for excellent

parts.note: excellent means fine

explanation.surface: A line of dialogue is slipped into a superb closing act.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing section of a show or opera is its finale, the last act or number.

clue.text: Great actor dropping one title role in musical

indicators.note: dropping tells us a letter falls out of the actor's name

parts.note: Laurence Olivier was a great English stage and screen actor
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A distinguished actor gives up a single starring part in a musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping one title' reads as losing a knighthood, but 'title role in musical' is the definition and 'one' is just I.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Twist is the title character of the musical Oliver!

clue.text: Rich countess in play taking capital from country

indicators.note: taking capital from means the first letter of the country is removed

parts.note: Bolivia is a South American country

explanation.surface: A wealthy noblewoman in a drama seizes a nation's capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests a city such as La Paz, but here it is the capital (first) letter of the country's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivia is the wealthy countess courted by Orsino in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night.

clue.text: I'm in China, doing a kind of acting

indicators.note: in places the first-person phrase inside the Chinese dynasty word

parts.note: Ming was a Chinese dynasty, famous for its porcelain
I'm gives its own letters, minus the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A traveller says they are in China, performing some sort of act.
explanation.definitionFit: Miming is wordless acting through gesture, a form of performance.

clue.text: Old London theatre that is, over short time, protected by dramatist

indicators.note: protected by means the inner pieces are enclosed by the dramatist's name

parts.note: John Gay was the dramatist who wrote The Beggar's Opera

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece above the next

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A historic London playhouse is described as sheltered by a playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gaiety was a famous London theatre on the Strand, known for musical comedy.

clue.text: Play seen in theatre of a musical guy's partner

parts.note: in the musical Guys and Dolls a guy's partner is a doll, here possessive
a house is a theatre, as in a full house

explanation.surface: A play is staged in the theatre belonging to a stage musical's leading man's girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre of a doll's' reads as a house belonging to a doll, so the phrase is reordered into the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibsen's drama about Nora Helmer is one of the best-known plays of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Playwright making appearance in group interview

indicators.note: making appearance in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dramatist turns up at a panel interview.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Pinter was a Nobel-winning English playwright, author of The Birthday Party.

clue.text: Like plays in which, after drink, I act atrociously

indicators.note: after says the rearranged letters come after the drink

parts.note: a dram is a small drink, especially of whisky

indicators.note: atrociously means very badly, so the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: An actor confesses that, after a whisky, their performance is dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Dramatic means relating to drama, of or like plays.

clue.text: Tragic heroine to imitate, coming to premature end

indicators.note: coming to premature end means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to mimic is to imitate

explanation.surface: Someone copies a doomed heroine until stopping too soon.
explanation.walkthrough: MIMIC loses its last letter, C. 'Premature end' fits the tragic heroine too, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimi is the consumptive seamstress who dies in Puccini's opera La Boheme.

clue.text: Outline for shadow play developed in hotel suite

indicators.note: developed means worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shadow-puppet show is worked up in a hotel room.
explanation.definitionFit: A silhouette is a dark outline shape, the image cast in shadow puppetry.

clue.text: Female introducing a speaker, possibly a playwright

indicators.note: introducing here means taking in, so the female word wraps the rest

parts.note: she is the female pronoun

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A woman presents an orator who might be a dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Introducing' means taking in here: the female pronoun wraps the scrambled speaker, and 'possibly' doubles as a hedge in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: William Shakespeare is the most famous playwright in English.

clue.text: Tragedy in which family, regal, gets destroyed

parts.note: kin means family

indicators.note: gets destroyed means the word is broken up and its letters rebuilt

explanation.surface: In a sad drama a royal family is brought to ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets destroyed' reads as the royal family's ruin, which is the plot of the play, but it only tells you to rearrange 'regal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's King Lear is one of his great tragedies.

clue.text: Again tries, with energy, to perform play in practice

parts.note: a court rehears a case when it tries it again
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A cast, rerunning things with vigour, practises staging a play.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to go through a play in practice before performing it.

clue.text: Group of people surrounding popular playwright

indicators.note: surrounding means the group word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a race is a group of people sharing descent
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A crowd gathers round a well-liked dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Racine was a French tragic playwright of the seventeenth century.

clue.text: Writer of drama for sanctimonious emperor

parts.note: pi is a slang shortening of pious, meaning sanctimonious
Nero was a Roman emperor

explanation.surface: A dramatist writes on behalf of a self-righteous ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Arthur Wing Pinero was an English writer of farces and dramas.

clue.text: Losing consciousness, so making an exit

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both fainting and literally going out through a door.

clue.text: Leading players seen around West End for openings

indicators.note: around means the players word encloses the letter

parts.note: the stars are the leading players in a show

indicators.note: End picks the final letter of West

explanation.surface: The principal performers are seen in London's theatre district on first nights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West End' reads as London's theatreland, but it just gives the last letter of West.
explanation.definitionFit: Starts are beginnings, so openings in the sense of commencements.

clue.text: Author of a play for voices, sceptical type

definitions.text: Author of a play for voices
definitions.meaning: Dylan ... wrote Under Milk Wood, subtitled a play for voices
a doubting person, after the apostle who doubted the resurrection

explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the Welsh poet is also the name for a habitual doubter, from doubting Thomas.

clue.text: Hard song to follow in old musical

indicators.note: to follow puts the song after the hard letter

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: A tough number comes next in a vintage stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair is the 1960s rock musical about hippie counterculture.

clue.text: Reclaims, in a way, subjects of old plays

indicators.note: in a way signals the letters are presented in another order

explanation.surface: Someone takes back, after a fashion, themes of early drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval miracle plays dramatised the miracles of saints.

clue.text: Dramatist in old suit appearing before end of play

parts.note: a case is a lawsuit

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of play

explanation.surface: A playwright in an ancient lawsuit turns up before a show finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sean O'Casey was the Irish dramatist of Juno and the Paycock.

clue.text: Minor actors in runs not resulting from hits

definitions.meaning: walk-on performers with small non-speaking parts
in cricket, runs scored from byes, wides and no-balls rather than off the bat

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket counts runs from wides, no-balls and byes, where the batter did not hit the ball, separately on the scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: Background performers and cricket's bonus runs share the same name, both being additions beyond the main work.

clue.text: Charlie I brought into company in part of lieutenant

indicators.note: brought into means the fool and I go inside the company abbreviation

parts.note: a charlie is British slang for a fool, an ass

explanation.surface: An actor named Charlie joins a troupe playing an officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' suggests C from the phonetic alphabet; here it is British slang for a fool, an ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassio is Othello's lieutenant in Shakespeare's tragedy.
